entries.title: Combat Order
entries.label: Combat
content: The DM determines surprise and starting positions, including where each side stands relative to the other. Everyone then rolls initiative.
Each participant takes a turn in initiative order. Once everyone has acted, begin another round in the same order if the fight continues. A round represents about 6 seconds.

entries.title: Surprise
entries.label: Combat
content: When one side tries to approach unnoticed, the DM compares the hiding creatures’ Dexterity (Stealth) checks with each opponent’s passive Wisdom (Perception). A creature that notices no threat is surprised. When neither side is trying to be stealthy, both sides notice each other.
Surprise is determined individually. A surprised creature cannot move or take an action or bonus action on its first turn, and it cannot react until that turn ends.

entries.title: Initiative
entries.label: Combat
content: At the start of combat, make a Dexterity check. Higher totals act earlier. The DM can use a single initiative roll for a group of identical creatures, which then act at the same initiative.

Players settle ties among their characters, and the DM settles ties among DM-controlled creatures and between the two sides. As an option, tied combatants can each roll a d20 and act in descending order of those rolls.

entries.title: Your Turn
entries.label: Combat
content: On your turn you normally get one action and movement up to your speed. Use them in either order, split up your movement, or skip either entirely.
You can make brief remarks or gestures during your turn when able. Ordinary object interactions and bonus actions have their own limits in the Action and Bonus Action categories.

entries.title: Movement in Combat
entries.label: Movement
content: Your speed sets how much movement you can use on your turn. You can combine walking, climbing, swimming, and jumping in one turn. Spend movement for each part at its applicable cost and stop when you are done or run out.

entries.title: Move
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 5ft per 5ft moved

If you have more than one speed, such as your walking speed and a flying speed, you can switch back and forth between your speeds during your move. Whenever you switch, subtract the distance you've already moved from the new speed.
You can move through a nonhostile creature's space.
You can move through a hostile creature's space only if the creature is at least two sizes larger or smaller than you.
Another creature's space is difficult terrain for you.
Whether a creature is a friend or an enemy, you can't willingly end your move in its space.
If subtracting the distance already moved leaves 0 or less for the new speed, you cannot move farther using that speed.

entries.title: Splitting Your Movement
entries.label: Movement
content: You can spend part of your movement before your action and the rest afterward. For example, with a 30-foot speed you can move 10 feet, take your action, then move another 20 feet.
An action that includes multiple weapon attacks also lets you move between those attacks, within the same movement budget.

entries.title: Climb
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 10ft per 5ft climbed
May involve a Strength (Athletics) check if the climb is difficult

entries.title: Swim
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 10ft per 5ft swum
May involve a Strength (Athletics) check if the swim is difficult

entries.title: Drop prone
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 0ft (free)
You can drop prone without using any of your speed
To move while prone, you must crawl or use magic such as teleportation
Dropping prone adds the
Prone
condition (melee attacks against you have advantage, ranged attacks against you have disadvantage, your own attacks have disadvantage)

entries.title: Crawl
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 10ft per 5ft crawled
Crawling through difficult terrain costs 15 feet of movement for every 5 feet travelled.

entries.title: Stand up
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: half of your speed
You can't stand up if you don't have enough movement left or if your speed is 0

entries.title: High jump
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 5ft per 5ft jumped
You leap into the air a number of feet equal to
3 + your Strength modifier
if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump.
When you make a standing high jump, you can jump only half that distance.
You can extend your arms half your height above yourself during the jump.
In some circumstances, your DM might allow you to make a Strength (Athletics) check to jump higher than you normally can.

entries.title: Long jump
entries.label: Movement

content: Movement cost: 5ft per 5ft jumped
You cover a number of feet up to your
Strength score
if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump.
When you make a standing long jump, you can leap only half that distance
May involve a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to clear a low obstacle (no taller than a quarter of the jump's distance). You hit the obstacle on a failed check.
May involve a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to land on your feet in difficult terrain. You land prone on a failed check.

entries.title: Improvise
entries.label: Movement

content: Perform any movement or stunt you can imagine
When you describe a kind of movement not detailed elsewhere in the rules, the DM tells you whether it is possible and what kind of roll you need to make, if any, to determine success or failure.

entries.title: Difficult terrain
entries.label: Movement

content: Moving in difficult terrain costs an additional 5ft per 5ft of movement
Several sources of difficult terrain in the same space do not increase the difficult-terrain cost again.

entries.title: Grapple move
entries.label: Movement

content: Drag or carry the grappled creature with you
If you move while grappling another creature, your speed is halved, unless the creature is two or more sizes smaller than you.
See the attack action for how to grapple a creature.

entries.title: Flying Movement
entries.label: Movement
content: A flying creature falls if it is knocked prone, its speed becomes 0, or it otherwise loses the ability to move. It stays aloft if it can hover or magic is holding it up, such as the Fly spell.

entries.title: Creature Space
entries.label: Movement
content: A creature’s space is the area it controls and needs to fight in. For instance, a Medium creature controls a 5-foot-wide space. See Creature Size under Fall Damage for the existing size table.

On a 5-foot grid, up to eight Medium creatures can surround another Medium creature. Larger creatures occupy more space, so fewer can fit around the same target. Size categories can also describe objects.

entries.title: Squeezing
entries.label: Movement
content: You can squeeze through a space that fits a creature one size smaller than you. A Large creature could therefore pass through a 5-foot-wide passage.
While squeezing, each foot moved costs 1 extra foot of movement. You have disadvantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws, and attacks against you have advantage.

entries.title: Actions in Combat
entries.label: Action
content: On your turn, spend your action on a standard action, an option granted by a class or other feature, or an improvised action. Monsters can also use options in their stat blocks.
For an improvised action, tell the DM what you want to do. The DM decides whether it is possible and whether you need a roll.

entries.title: Fortification
entries.label: Action

content: Focus your vein of magic on incoming magical effects
Until the start of your next turn, any magical attack roll made against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make saving throws agains magic with advantage.
You lose this benefit if you are
incapacitated
deafened
or when you use
Absorb
reaction.
Additionaly if you have spell casting ability score more than 22 you can use special Absorb reaction while in Fortification.

When you are targeted by a single target or area of spell, even if you manage to avoid the spell effect, you can use your reaction to Absorb the spell. This will restore your lowest level empty spell slot and heal you for your profficiency bonus times the level of resotered spell slot.

entries.title: Attack
entries.label: Action

content: Perform a melee or ranged attack with your weapon
Certain features, such as the
Extra Attack
feature of the fighter, allow you to make more than one attack with this action. Each of these attacks is a separate roll and may target different creatures. You may move in between these attacks.
When you attack with a light melee weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with your other hand (see the
Offhand attack
bonus action).
You may replace Action with
Shove
Grapple
or
Toss

Some conditions give advantage on the attack: attacks against blinded, paralyzed, petrified, restrained, stunned, or unconscious targets; melee attacks against prone targets; attacks by invisible or hidden attackers.
Some conditions give disadvantage on the attack: attacks against invisible or hidden targets; ranged attacks against prone targets; attacks by blinded, frightened, poisoned, or restrained attackers.

entries.title: Non-Lethal Damage
entries.label: Action sub-type

content: Before making an attack or casting a damaging spell, a creature can declare its intention to incapacitate rather than kill.
Non-lethal attacks are more difficult to execute:
Damage remains unchanged. If a non-lethal attack reduces a creature to 0 HP, it falls unconscious and stable instead of dying.
Spells that explicitly kill or destroy their targets, such as Power Word Kill or Disintegrate, cannot be used non-lethally.
For area-of-effect spells, the reduced Spell Save DC applies to all affected creatures.

entries.title: Grapple
entries.label: Action

content: Attempt to grab a creature or wrestle with it
You can use the Attack Action to make a special melee attack, a grapple. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them but not multiple of them.
The target of your grapple must be no more than one size larger than you, and it must be within your reach.

Using at least one free hand, you try to seize the target by making a grapple check, a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use).
If you succeed, you subject the target to the grappled condition (its speed is set to 0).
You may release a creature you are grappling at any time without spending an action.

entries.title: Toss
entries.label: Action

content: Attempt to toss grappled creature

If you have Strenght score more than 22 you can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack, Toss, on the creature you hold in grapple. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them but not multiple of them. (Still means you can use Grepple and Toss on same turn.)
You can toss the creature up to a distance equal to 5 feet per 2 points of your Strength modifier (With 6 Strenght modifier it would be 5*(6/2) -> 15 feet).
The creature suffers falling damage based on the distance tossed and where it lands. It also must succeed on Dexterity saving throw (DC = Distance traveled) or will land prone.

If you toss the creature into another creature (target), target creature must succeed on Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + proficiency bonus) or will take same damage as tossed creature, in success no damage is dealt.

If you toss the creature into environmental hazard it will take damage depending on the type of hazard (determined by the DM). Example, Spikes, will deal one time damage durring the toss, while flames will deal overtime damage on creatures turn.

entries.title: Shove
entries.label: Action

content: Shove a creature, either to knock it prone or push it away from you

Using the Attack action, you can make a special melee attack to shove a creature. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this attack replaces one of them but not multiple of them.
The target of your shove must be no more than one size larger than you, and it must be within your reach.
You make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use).
If you win the contest, you either knock the target prone or push it 5 feet away from you or to the side.

entries.title: Cast a spell
entries.label: Action

content: Cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action
You can't cast a spell with you action and a different spell with your bonus action in the same turn, except if the action is used to cast a cantrip.
The target of a spell must be within the spell's range. To target something, you must have a clear path to it, so it can't be behind total cover.

Spells with material components do not consume the material unless explicitly stated. Unless the cost of a material is given, you can assume that the cost is negligible and the material is simply available in a component pouch.

Some spells require you to maintain concentration in order to keep their magic active. If you lose concentration, such a spell ends. You lose concentration on a spell if you cast another spell that requires concentration or when you are incapacitated. Each time you take damage, you must make a Constitution saving throw to maintain your concentration. The DC equals 10 or half the damage you take, whichever number is higher.
The spell’s casting time determines which action, bonus action, or reaction it uses, or whether it takes longer to cast. A spell with a casting time of 1 action uses your action.

entries.title: Dash
entries.label: Action

content: Gain extra movement for the current turn
The increase equals your speed, after applying any modifiers.
If your speed changes during the turn, adjust the extra movement from Dash by the same amount. For example, a speed reduced from 30 to 15 feet gives you 30 feet of total movement with Dash.
Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn

entries.title: Dodge
entries.label: Action

content: Focus entirely on avoiding attacks
Until the start of your next turn, any weapon attack roll made against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with advantage.
You lose this benefit if you are
incapacitated
or if your speed drops to 0.

entries.title: Escape
entries.label: Action

content: Escape a grapple
To escape a grapple, you must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the grappler's Strength (Athletics) check.
Escaping other conditions that restrain you (such as manacles) may require a Dexterity or Strength check, as specified by the condition.

entries.title: Help
entries.label: Action

content: Grant an ally advantage on an ability check (if you have the know-how [proff. or expt.] with the ability) or attack
The target gains advantage on the next ability check it makes to perform the task you are helping with.
Alternatively, the target gains advantage on the next attack roll against a creature within 5 feet of you.
The advantage lasts until the start of your next turn.

entries.title: Use Object
entries.label: Action

content: Interact with a second object or use special object abilities
You can interact with one object for free during your turn (such as drawing a weapon or opening a door). If you want to interact with a second object, use this action.
When an object requires your action for its use, you also take this action.

The free interaction can happen during your move or action. Drawing or sheathing a weapon, pulling an ordinary lever, or handing someone an item are common examples. The DM can require an action for an interaction that needs unusual effort or care, such as forcing a stuck mechanism.

entries.title: Use shield
entries.label: Action

content: Equip or unequip a shield
A shield always takes an action to equip or unequip.
Armor takes several minutes to equip or unequip.

entries.title: Hide
entries.label: Action

content: Attempt to hide
You can't hide from a creature that can see you. You must have total cover, be in a heavily obscured area, be invisible, or otherwise block the enemy's vision.
If you make noise (such as shouting a warning or knocking over a vase), you give away your position.

When you try to hide, make a Dexterity (Stealth) check and note the result. Until you are discovered or you stop hiding, that check's total is contested by the Wisdom (Perception) check of any creature that actively searches for signs of your presence.
A creature notices you even if it isn't searching unless your Stealth check is higher than its Passive Perception.

Out of combat, you may also use a Dexterity (Stealth) check for acts like concealing yourself from enemies, slinking past guards, slipping away without being noticed, or sneaking up on someone without being seen or heard.

entries.title: Search
entries.label: Action

content: Devote your attention to finding something
Depending on the nature of your search, the DM might have you make a Wisdom (Perception) check or an Intelligence (Investigation) check.

entries.title: Ready
entries.label: Action

content: Choose a trigger and a response reaction
First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your reaction.
Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your speed in response to it.
When the trigger occurs, you can either take your reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger.

When you ready a spell, you cast it as normal but hold its energy, which you release with your reaction when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a spell must have a casting time of 1 action, and holding onto the spell's magic requires concentration.
Additionaly if you have Strength or Dexterity score more than 18 you, can use your available extra attacks as part of the readied Attack action.

The readied response is available only until the start of your next turn and uses your reaction. If you lose concentration before releasing a readied spell, the spell dissipates without taking effect.
Use a racial or class feature that uses an action

entries.title: Stabilize a creature
entries.label: Action

content: Stop a dying creature from needing to make death saving throws
Make a Wisdom (Medicine) check with DC 10
On a success, the creature is stable and no longer needs to make death saving throws
A stable creature regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours

entries.title: Climb onto a Bigger Creature
entries.label: Action

content: Get to unexpected position

If one creature wants to jump onto another creature, it can do so by grappling. A small or Medium creature has little chance of making a successful grapple against a Huge or Gargantuan creature, however, unless magic has granted the grappler supernatural might.

As an alternative, a suitably large opponent can be treated as terrain for the purpose of jumping onto its back or clinging to a limb. After making any ability checks necessary to get into position and onto the larger creature, the smaller creature uses its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the target's Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. If it wins the contest, the smaller creature successfully moves into the target creature's space, the smaller creature moves with the target and has advantage on attack rolls against it.

The smaller creature can move around within the larger creature's space, treating the space as difficult terrain. The larger creature's ability to attack the smaller creature depends on the smaller creature's location, and is left to your discretion. The larger creature can dislodge the smaller creature as an action—knocking it off, scraping it against a wall, or grabbing and throwing it—by making a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the smaller creature's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. The smaller creature chooses which ability to use.

entries.title: Disarm
entries.label: Action

content: Remove the opponents weapon

A creature can use a weapon attack to knock a weapon or another item from a target's grasp. The attacker makes an attack roll contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) check or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. If the attacker wins the contest, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but the defender drops the item.

The attacker has disadvantage on its attack roll if the target is holding the item with two or more hands. The target has advantage on its ability check if it is larger than the attacking creature, or disadvantage if it is smaller.

entries.title: Overrun
entries.label: Action

content: Run across occupied space with brute force

When a creature tries to move through a hostile creature's space, the mover can try to force its way through by overrunning the hostile creature. As an action or a bonus action, the mover makes a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the hostile creature's Strength (Athletics) check. The creature attempting the overrun has advantage on this check if it is larger than the hostile creature, or disadvantage if it is smaller. If the mover wins the contest, it can move through the hostile creature's space once this turn.

entries.title: Tumble
entries.label: Action

content: Run across occupied space with skill

A creature can try to tumble through a hostile creature's space, ducking and weaving past the opponent. As an action or a bonus action, the tumbler makes a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the hostile creature's Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. If the tumbler wins the contest, it can move through the hostile creature's space once this turn.

entries.title: Tie Up
entries.label: Action

content: Attempt to bind a creature with rope or similar restraints.
You can use your action to tie up a creature that is Grappled or Unconscious. You must have suitable binding materials and be within your reach of the target.
If the target is Grappled, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use).
If you succeed, the target is subjected to the Bound condition. On a failure, the target remains Grappled but is not Bound.
If the target is Unconscious, you can tie it up without making a contested check. The target automatically gains the Bound condition.

entries.title: Improvise
entries.label: Action

content: Perform any action you can imagine
When you describe an action not detailed elsewhere in the rules, the DM tells you whether that action is possible and what kind of roll you need to make, if any, to determine success or failure.

entries.title: Bonus Actions
entries.label: Bonus Action
content: You can take a bonus action only if a spell, feature, or other rule gives you one. You can use at most one on your turn, even if you have several options.
Choose when during your turn to use it unless the option specifies a timing or prerequisite. If you cannot take actions, you also cannot take bonus actions.

entries.title: Offhand Attack
entries.label: Bonus Action

content: Attack with your off hand
Only usable if you take the
Attack
action and attack with a light melee weapon that you're holding in one hand.
Perform a single attack with a different light melee weapon that you're holding in the other hand.
You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.
If either weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon, instead of making a melee attack with it.

entries.title: Cast a spell
entries.label: Bonus Action

content: Cast a spell with a casting time of 1 bonus action
You can't cast a spell with you action and a different spell with your bonus action in the same turn, except if the action is used to cast a cantrip.
For further details, see the
Cast a spell
action.
Use a racial or class feature that uses a bonus action

entries.title: Reactions
entries.label: Reaction
content: A reaction responds to a specified trigger on your turn or someone else’s. After using one, you get it back at the start of your next turn.
If your reaction interrupts another creature’s turn, that creature continues its turn once the reaction resolves. Follow the timing specified by the trigger.

entries.title: Vykrytie
entries.label: Reaction

content: You have the ability to nullify critical weapon attacks at the cost of your weapons durability
Trigger: When you wield a weapon you're proficient with and an enemy creature you can see scores a Critical Hit with weapon attack against you.
Your weapon loses one durability and the enemy attack becomes regular attack.

If your weapon possesses the Hulking property, you can engage in an Athletics check contested by the attacker's Athletics or Acrobatics check. Succeeding in this contest negates the damage from the attack, while failure results in your weapon losing two durabilities instead of one.

If your weapon possesses the Exquisite property, you can engage in an Acrobatics check contested by the attacker's Athletics or Acrobatics check. Succeeding in this contest allows you to successfully counterattack the assailant, rolling damage. However, failing results in your weapon losing two durabilities instead of one.
If your weapon possesses both the Hulking and Exquisite properties, you must choose to utilize only one of them for the purpose of this reaction.

entries.title: Opportunity attack
entries.label: Reaction

content: You can rarely move heedlessly past your foes without putting yourself in danger
Trigger: enemy creature you can see leaves your reach.
Make one melee attack against the provoking creature.
The attack interrupts the provoking creature's movement, occurring right before the creature leaves your reach.
Creatures don't provoke an opportunity attack when they teleport or when someone or something moves them without using their movement, action, or reaction.

entries.title: Readied action
entries.label: Reaction

content: Execute the reaction specified by your Ready action
Trigger: specified by your
Ready
action.

entries.title: Cast a spell
entries.label: Reaction

content: Cast a spell with a casting time of 1 reaction
Trigger: specified by the spell.
For further details, see the
Cast a spell
action.

entries.title: Making an Attack
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: Pick a creature, object, or location within the attack’s reach or range. Determine cover, advantage or disadvantage, and any other modifiers before rolling.
Make the attack roll. A hit normally deals damage, and the attack can also specify additional effects or substitute an effect for damage.
An attack roll counts as an attack. Special attacks such as grappling and shoving use the contests described in their own entries.

entries.title: Attack Rolls
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: Roll a d20 and add the applicable attack modifiers. The attack hits if its total meets or exceeds the target’s Armor Class.

Melee weapon attacks normally use Strength, ranged weapon attacks normally use Dexterity, and spell attacks use the caster’s spellcasting ability. Finesse and thrown weapons follow their weapon properties.
Add proficiency if you are proficient with the weapon or making a spell attack. Monsters normally use the attack bonus listed in their stat blocks.

entries.title: Natural 1 and Natural 20
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: A natural 1 on an attack roll misses regardless of the total. A natural 20 hits regardless of the target’s AC and scores a critical hit. See Critical Hits under Damage & Healing for the damage roll.

entries.title: Unseen Attackers and Targets
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: Attacking a target you cannot see gives you disadvantage, even if you can hear it. If you aim at the wrong location, you miss. The DM can report the miss without confirming where the target is.
You have advantage against a target that cannot see you. If you were hidden from the target, your attack reveals your location whether it hits or misses.

entries.title: Melee Attacks and Reach
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: A melee attack can target something within your reach. Most creatures have a 5-foot reach, though particular weapons, creature attacks, and features can specify a different reach. Some spells also call for melee attacks.

entries.title: Unarmed Strikes
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: You can make a melee weapon attack by punching, kicking, or striking with your body. You are proficient with your unarmed strikes.

On a hit, a basic unarmed strike deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1 + your Strength modifier, to a minimum of 0. Features can change the damage or the ability used. An unarmed strike does not use a weapon.

entries.title: Ranged Attacks and Range
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: An attack with one listed range cannot reach beyond it. If two distances are listed, the first is the normal range and the second is the maximum range.
Attacks beyond normal range have disadvantage. You cannot attack a target beyond the maximum range.

entries.title: Ranged Attacks in Close Combat
entries.label: Attack Rules
content: A ranged attack roll has disadvantage if a hostile creature within 5 feet of you can see you and is not incapacitated. This applies to ranged spell attacks as well as ranged weapon attacks. The nearby creature can be different from the target.

entries.title: Hit Points
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Current hit points range from 0 to your hit point maximum. Damage reduces current hit points. Losing hit points by itself does not impair you before you reach 0.

entries.title: Damage Rolls
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Use the dice and modifiers specified by the attack or effect. Damage cannot drop below 0. A weapon attack usually adds the ability modifier used for its attack roll. Follow any exception in the attack or feature, such as Offhand Attack.
If one effect deals damage to several targets simultaneously, roll the damage once and apply each target’s own saves, resistance, or other modifiers to that result.

entries.title: Critical Hits
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Roll twice the normal number of damage dice for the attack, including extra dice such as Sneak Attack. Add flat modifiers once. For example, a critical hit that normally deals 1d8 + 3 deals 2d8 + 3.

entries.title: Standard Damage Types
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Use the type named by the attack or effect. This table lists the standard 5e types. Axria features may also refer to campaign-specific damage categories.

entries.title: Resistance and Vulnerability
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Resistance halves damage of the specified type, rounding down. Vulnerability doubles it. Apply other damage modifiers first, then resistance, then vulnerability.
Overlapping sources of resistance to the same damage apply only once. The same limit applies to vulnerability. For example, 25 damage reduced by 5 before resistance becomes 10 damage.

entries.title: Healing
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Add healing to your current hit points, up to your hit point maximum. Any amount beyond the maximum is lost. Rest, spells, and potions can restore hit points as their rules specify.
A dead creature must first be restored to life before it can regain hit points.

entries.title: Instant Death from Massive Damage
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: When a hit takes a creature to 0 HP, compare the leftover damage with its hit point maximum. If the leftover damage reaches or exceeds that maximum, the creature dies immediately.
For example, a creature with 6 current HP and a maximum of 12 dies instantly if it takes 18 damage. If the hit does not kill the creature outright, see Dying under Condition.

entries.title: Monsters at 0 HP
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: The DM usually treats ordinary monsters as dead when they drop to 0 HP. A major villain or other important NPC can instead fall unconscious and use the campaign’s Dying rules. See Non-Lethal Damage when an attacker deliberately aims to incapacitate.

entries.title: Temporary Hit Points
entries.label: Damage & Healing
content: Temporary HP absorb damage before your regular HP. For example, if you have 5 temporary HP and take 7 damage, you lose the 5 temporary HP and 2 regular HP.

Temporary HP are tracked separately from regular HP, can put your combined total above your normal maximum, and cannot be restored by healing. If you receive more while you still have some, choose which pool to keep.

At 0 regular HP, temporary HP can still absorb damage. Receiving them does not stabilize you or wake you up. Unless the source specifies a duration, they last until spent or until you finish a long rest.

entries.title: Eligible Mounts
entries.label: Mounted Combat
content: A willing creature can serve as a mount if its anatomy allows it and it is at least one size larger than the rider.

entries.title: Mounting and Dismounting
entries.label: Mounted Combat
content: Once during your move you can mount a creature within 5 feet or dismount. Either costs movement equal to half your speed. Your speed must be above 0 and you must have enough movement left.

entries.title: Falling from a Mount
entries.label: Mounted Combat
content: If your mount is moved against its will while you are riding, or if you are knocked prone while mounted, make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you fall off and land prone within 5 feet of the mount.
If the mount itself falls prone, you can spend your reaction to dismount and land on your feet. Otherwise you land prone within 5 feet of it.

entries.title: Controlled and Independent Mounts
entries.label: Mounted Combat
content: You can control a mount trained to accept a rider. When you mount it, its initiative matches yours. It moves as you direct, can move and act on the turn you mount it, and can choose only Dash, Disengage, or Dodge as its action.
An independent mount keeps its initiative and its own action options. It moves and acts as it chooses. Intelligent mounts such as dragons act independently.
If either kind of mount provokes an opportunity attack while you are riding it, the attacker can choose the rider or the mount as the target.

entries.title: Blinded
entries.label: Condition

content: You can't see
You automatically fail any ability check which requires sight.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.

entries.title: Charmed
entries.label: Condition

content: You are charmed by another creature
You can't attack your charmer or target them with harmful abilities or magical effects.
Your charmer has advantage on ability checks to interact socially with you.

entries.title: Deafened
entries.label: Condition

content: You can't hear
You automatically fail any ability check which requires hearing.

entries.title: Exhaustion
entries.label: Condition

content: Exhaustion is measured in six levels

rows: Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

content: You suffer the effect of your current level of exhaustion as well as all lower levels.
Finishing a long rest reduces your exhaustion level by 1, provided that you have also had some food and drink.
Also, being raised from the dead reduces a creature’s exhaustion level by 1.

entries.title: Frightened
entries.label: Condition

content: You are frightened
You have disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of your fear is within line of sight.
You can't willingly move closer to the source of your fear.

entries.title: Grappled
entries.label: Condition

content: You are grappled
Your speed becomes 0, and you can't benefit from any bonus to your speed.
The condition ends if your grappler is incapacitated.
The condition also ends if you are removed from the reach of your grappler.
You can't take actions or reactions

entries.title: Invisible
entries.label: Condition

content: You can't be seen without the aid of magic or a special sense
For the purpose of hiding, you are heavily obscured.
You can still be detected by any noise you make or tracks you leave.
You have advantage on attack rolls.
Attack rolls against you have disadvantage.

entries.title: Paralyzed
entries.label: Condition

content: You can't do anything
You are incapacitated and can't move or speak.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.
Any attack that hits you is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.
You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.title: Petrified
entries.label: Condition

content: You are transformed, along with any nonmagical objects you are wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone)
Your weight increases by a factor of ten, and you cease aging.
You are incapacitated, can't move or speak, and are unaware of your surroundings.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.
You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
You have resistance to all damage.
You are immune to poison and disease, though a poison or disease already in your system is only suspended, not neutralized.

entries.title: Poisoned
entries.label: Condition

content: You are poisoned
You have disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

entries.title: Prone
entries.label: Condition

content: You are prone
Your only movement option is to crawl, unless you stand up.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls.
Attack rolls against you have advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of you, otherwise the attack roll has disadvantage.

entries.title: Restrained
entries.label: Condition

content: You are restrained
Your speed becomes 0, and you can't benefit from any bonus to your speed.
You have disadvantage on attack rolls.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.
You have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

entries.title: Stunned
entries.label: Condition

content: You are stunned
You are incapacitated, can't move, and can speak only falteringly.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.
You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.title: Frostbitten
entries.label: Condition

content: You are partially frozen
You have disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
Your speed is halved.

entries.title: Overheated
entries.label: Condition

content: You body is overheating
You have disadvantage on Strength and Intelligence saving throws.
You cannot take reactions.

entries.title: Disoriented
entries.label: Condition

content: You feel dizzy and slighly confused
The creature can’t take the Dash action or benefit from any movement speed bonuses.
When the creature makes an attack and has more than one valid target in sight, it must 1d6, on 1 it hits the the nearest target other then the main target.

entries.title: Unconscious
entries.label: Condition

content: You are unconscious
You are incapacitated, can't move or speak, and are unaware of your surroundings.
You drop whatever you're holding and fall prone.
Attack rolls against you have advantage.
Any attack that hits you is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.
You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.title: Suffocating
entries.label: Condition

content: Out of breath and suffocating
A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds).

When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it can survive for a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 round). At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying, and it can’t regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again.

entries.title: Bound
entries.label: Condition

content: A creature secured by rope, chains, or similar restraints.
A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds).
A Bound creature cannot use limbs that are tied or otherwise secured.
If both its arms and legs are bound, the creature also suffers the Restrained condition.
A Bound creature can use its action to attempt a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the original binder's Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) result (minimum DC 10). On a success, it escapes the bindings.
A creature can instead use its action to attempt a Strength check to break DC 20 ordinary ropes or DC 30 for ordinary chains.
Another creature within reach can use its action to untie the bindings without a check.

entries.title: Dying
entries.label: Condition

content: You have been dropped to zero hit points and are dying
If you are reduced to 0 hit points by damage that fails to kill you, you fall unconscious and are dying.
If you receive any healing you immediately regain consciousness again and no longer dying.
When dying, at the start of each of your turns you make a death saving throw. Roll a d20 and do not add any modifiers.
A 10 or higher is a success, 9 or lower is a failure.
On your third success, you become stable.
On your third failure, you die.
Rolling a 1 counts as two failures.
Rolling a 20 counts as two successes.
You can also be stabilized by an ally taking the Stabilize action and succeeding on a DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check.
Once stable, you regain 1 hit point after 1d4 hours.
Successes and failures are tracked separately and need not be consecutive. Reset both counts when you regain hit points or become stable.
Damage taken at 0 HP adds one death save failure, or two if it comes from a critical hit. If that damage equals or exceeds your hit point maximum, you die outright.
A stable creature at 0 HP remains unconscious. If it takes damage, it loses stability and must resume death saves if it survives.

entries.title: Lightly obscured
entries.label: Environment obscurance

content: Dim light, patchy fog, moderate foliage
Creatures have
disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception)
checks that rely on sight.

entries.title: Heavily obscured
entries.label: Environment obscurance

content: Darkness, opaque fog, dense foliage
A creature in a heavily obscured area effectively suffers from the
blinded condition

entries.title: Bright light
entries.label: Environment light

content: Bright light lets most creatures see normally
Gloomy days still provide bright light, as do torches, lanterns, fires, and other sources of illumination within a specific radius.

entries.title: Dim light
entries.label: Environment light

content: Dim light, also called shadows
Creates a
lightly obscured
area.
An area of dim light is usually a boundary between a source of bright light, such as a torch, and surrounding darkness.
The soft light of twilight and dawn also counts as dim light. A particularly brilliant full moon might bathe the land in dim light.

entries.title: Darkness
entries.label: Environment light

content: Darkness creates a heavily obscured area
Creates a
heavily obscured
area.
Characters face darkness outdoors at night (even most moonlit nights), within the confines of an unlit dungeon or a subterranean vault, or in an area of magical darkness.

entries.title: Blindsight
entries.label: Environment vision

content: Perceive your surroundings without relying on sight, within a certain radius
Creatures without eyes, such as oozes, and creatures with echolocation or heightened senses, such as bats and true dragons, have this sense.

entries.title: Darkvision
entries.label: Environment vision

content: A creature with Darkvision can see better in the dark or low light conditions, within a certain radius
Within a specified range, a creature with darkvision can
see in darkness as if the darkness were dim light
, so areas of darkness are only lightly obscured as far as that creature is concerned.
However, the creature can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.
Many creatures in the worlds of D&D, especially those that dwell underground, have darkvision.

entries.title: Arcsight
entries.label: Environment vision

content: A creature with Arcsight can see active magic on objects or creatures they can already see with thier sight

Within a specified range, a creature with arcsight can see traces of magic on magical objects, magical aura around places affected by magic or active magic on creature. They can also distinguish if certain effect was caused by magic or not.
However, the creature can’t discern school of magic or its purpose.
Most of high level Intelligence casters have Arcsight, how ever it can also be common for monsters.

entries.title: Truesight
entries.label: Environment vision

content: A creature with truesight can see everything in its true form, independent of the environment

A creature with truesight can, out to a specific range, see in normal and magical darkness, see invisible creatures and objects, automatically detect visual illusions and succeed on saving throws against them, and perceives the original form of a shapechanger or a creature that is transformed by magic.
Furthermore, the creature can see into the Ethereal Plane.

entries.title: Cover and Line of Attack
entries.label: Environment Effects
content: Cover protects a target when an obstacle stands between it and the source of an attack or other effect. Cover can therefore differ depending on the attacker’s position.

entries.title: Half cover
entries.label: Environment cover

content: A target has half cover if an obstacle blocks at least half of its body
The obstacle might be a low wall, a large piece of furniture, a narrow tree trunk, or a creature, whether that creature is an enemy or a friend.
A target with half cover has a
+2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws
If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies
Half cover applies when the obstacle blocks at least half the target’s body.

entries.title: Three-quarters cover
entries.label: Environment cover

content: A target has three-quarters cover if about three-quarters of it is covered by an obstacle
The obstacle might be a portcullis, an arrow slit, or a thick tree trunk.
A target with three-quarters cover has a
+5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws
If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies
Three-quarters cover applies when the obstacle blocks roughly three quarters of the target’s body.

entries.title: Full cover
entries.label: Environment cover

content: A target has total cover if it is completely concealed by an obstacle
A target with total cover
can’t be targeted directly
by an attack or a spell, although some spells can reach such a target by including it in an area of effect.
If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree of cover applies
Total cover applies when an obstacle completely blocks the target from the source of the attack or effect.

entries.title: Underwater Melee Attacks
entries.label: Environment Effects
content: Underwater, melee weapon attacks made without a swimming speed have disadvantage. Daggers, javelins, shortswords, spears, and tridents are exceptions. A swimming speed can be natural or granted by magic.

entries.title: Underwater Ranged Attacks
entries.label: Environment Effects
content: A ranged weapon attack underwater automatically misses beyond the weapon’s normal range. Within normal range, it has disadvantage unless you use a crossbow, a net, or a weapon thrown like a javelin, such as a spear, trident, or dart.

entries.title: Fire Damage Underwater
entries.label: Environment Effects
content: Fully submerged creatures and objects have resistance to fire damage.

entries.title: Fall Damage
entries.label: Fall Damage
content: Fall speed is 190feet per round. Damage then depends on both height and weight of the fallen creature/object. Heavy creatures/objects can create aura of Fear and cause creatures to become Frightened of the impacted locattion. Creatures Frightened in such way will stay Frightened untill they will pass the saving throw at the end of their turn or untill few days since passed.

Impact point is always the space covered by size of creature/object. This is where fall damage is dealt to both fallen craeture/object and the creatures, objects or anything else in the area. Heavy objects can also create area around intial impact point. This area is marked in table and each creature, obejct or anything else in area will receive third of the fall damage.

entries.title: Language

rows: Unknown; unmapped outer planes & distant entities

content: Language notes
Common Dialects

Innumerable Dialects. Each major city has at least 60 dialects, frequently shaped by mixed heritage and subtle blending of Common with ancestral racial languages. Most are mutually intelligible; variation appears in accents, turns of phrase, and names for particular objects. Speakers may not notice the difference until a single unfamiliar word comes up. There is no practical exhaustive list.
Clan Languages

No Uniform Standard. Typically descended from Common or Elder Common. No two clans speak exactly alike. Differences may involve vocabulary, sentence order, grammar, or strongly guttural sounds. One clan may sound like a familiar Common dialect; another may be effectively unintelligible to outsiders. “Clan Language” is a cultural classification, not a fixed degree of divergence.
Elder Common
Elder Common An ancient, extinct ancestral tongue. It no longer has living native-speaker communities; traces survive in texts, inscriptions, and languages descended from it.
Deep Speech
Deep Speech Of unknown origin, tied only to mysterious outer planes, distant entities, and unmapped locations. It has no established home plane, people, or known script.
Trinaria

Binary with Symbolic Nodes, know as Kraftografi. Binary can represent the complete and exact meaning of any message, but long sequences are inefficient. Nodes are unique symbols that encapsulate full binary meaning into compact, reusable representations (objects, directions, actions, or complex instructions). Nodes improve speed and communication with non-Apparatus beings; they do not discard information. Pure binary remains sufficient within Apparatus.
Primordial

Primordial can be split into 5 mian dialects. Aquan - Water, Auran - Air, Ignan - Fire, Terran - Earth, Boltan - Lightning. There are also sub-categories to each which mostly reside in the planes between elements. But those 5 are the main ones which can be often encountered in the Axria as well.
